questions.def: "It" is used as a dummy subject introducing the main idea.
questions.question: ___ is important to consider all options before deciding.

questions.def: "There" introduces the existence of something.
questions.question: ___ seems to be a problem with the network connection.

questions.def: "There appears" indicates existence and agrees in number.
questions.question: ___ to be some confusion about the meeting time.

questions.def: "It" is used as a dummy subject for impersonal constructions.
questions.question: ___ is believed that the suspect has left the country.

questions.def: "There's" indicates a lack of reason or purpose.
questions.question: ___'s no point in arguing about it now.

questions.def: The correct construction is "It is obvious that...".
questions.question: There is obvious that he is lying again.

questions.def: "It seems" introduces an impersonal observation.
questions.question: ___ that everyone has forgotten about the deadline.

questions.def: "It" is a dummy subject, the real subject is 'to admit'.
questions.question: ___ takes courage to admit when you are wrong.

questions.def: "There are" indicates the existence of multiple items.
questions.question: ___ are several factors contributing to the problem.

questions.def: "It is" introduces a statement of fact or opinion.
questions.question: ___ a great honor to receive this award.

questions.def: "It" refers to the weather.
questions.question: ___ is raining heavily, so take an umbrella.

questions.def: "There used to be" indicates past existence.
questions.question: ___ used to be a cinema here.

questions.def: "It takes" expresses the duration of an activity.
questions.question: ___ a long time to get used to the new software.

questions.def: "There is no" indicates an absence of something.
questions.question: ___ is no evidence to support his claims.

questions.def: "There is a possibility" introduces a potential event.
questions.question: ___ is a possibility that the flight will be delayed.

questions.def: "It is my opinion" is the correct expression.
questions.question: There is my opinion that we should wait.

questions.def: "It is difficult" expresses a challenging situation.
questions.question: ___ difficult to find a parking spot downtown.

questions.def: "It" acts as a placeholder for the infinitive phrase.
questions.question: ___ is essential to have a valid passport for international travel.

questions.def: "There are times" indicates specific instances.
questions.question: ___ are times when I miss my old job.

questions.def: "It seems" introduces an observation about a situation.
questions.question: ___ that the problem has been resolved.

questions.def: "There is" introduces something that exists.
questions.question: ___ is a great view from the top of the mountain.

questions.def: "It" is used to introduce the importance of something.
questions.question: ___ is important to be punctual for meetings.

questions.def: "There appears" indicates the lack of a solution.
questions.question: ___ to be no easy solution to this problem.

questions.def: "It is said" introduces a common saying or belief.
questions.question: ___ is said that honesty is the best policy.

questions.def: "There is likely to be" indicates a probability.
questions.question: ___ is likely to be a traffic jam on the highway.

questions.def: Use 'It' as a dummy subject when the real subject is a 'to' infinitive.
questions.question: ___ is important to consider all options before deciding.

questions.def: Use 'There' to indicate the existence of something, followed by 'appears'.
questions.question: ___ appears to be a misunderstanding regarding the new policy.

questions.def: 'It is believed' is a common impersonal passive construction.
questions.question: ___ ___ that the company will succeed despite challenges.

questions.def: 'There seems to be' indicates existence. 'To be' is the infinitive.
questions.question: ___ seems ___ be no easy solution to this complex problem.

questions.def: 'There was a time' indicates existence of a past period; indefinite article 'a'.
questions.question: ___ was ___ time when I enjoyed working on weekends.
